facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal document describes Chad's civil registration processes as predominantly paper-based and cumbersome, with a transition from them still ahead; the passage is undated, so the document's date is used.

The appraisal document states that the government, with UNICEF support and EU funding, is currently setting up birth registration kiosks equipped with digital tools in eleven health centres in N'Djamena; undated, so the document's date is used.
facts.system: Birth registration kiosks in health centres

facts.fact: The birth registration kiosks in eleven N'Djamena health centres are being set up by the government with support from UNICEF using EU funding; no domestic budget line is stated. Undated, so the document's date is used.

facts.fact: The appraisal document names the Government of Chad as the party setting up the birth registration kiosks, with UNICEF in support; undated, so the document's date is used.

The kiosks are being set up, not reported in service, so no offices fact is taken; they are classed civil on the document's words that they are birth registration points with digital tools. The project (US$120m, IDA grant of US$92.2m) states an intention to modernise the civil registry system, with no system named in these passages.
